full_judgment:
6. Under the circumstances, the petitioners filed this writ petition and obtained the present rule on the ground that the 2nd execution case having not been filed within 6 years from the date of filing of the execution case as required under section 28 (4) of the Artha Rin Ain 2003 it is barred by limitation and therefore, the execution proceeding as well as the impugned order is without lawful authority. 

 8. Mr. Abdul Barek Chowdhury, the learned Advocate for the petitioners has taken us through the writ petition including the various annexes thereto and the impugned order annexed to the application for injunction and submits that for realisation of the decretal amount of Title Suit No. 261 of 1998 the 1st Execution Case No 24 of 2001 was instituted on 14.3.2001 which was renumbered as Artha Jari Case No. 488 of 2003 before the Adalat and the said execution case was disposed of on 28.6.2007. He next submits that the 2nd execution case was filed on 27.6.2007 after expiry of the period of 6 years from the date of filing of the 1st execution case as provided in section 28 (4) of the Ain, 2003 and as the 2nd execution case was filed beyond the period of 6 years it was barred by limitation and so, the proceeding of the entire execution case as well as the impugned order dated 12.5.2009 for civil imprisonment and for issuing warrant of arrest against the petitioners are without lawful authority and liable to be struck down. 

 10. In reply, Mr. Md. Mujibur Rahman Meah, the learned Advocate for respondent No. 3 (the Bank) contends that the 1st execution case was filed on 14.3.2001 for execution of decree of Title Suit No. 261 of 1998 and the Ain, 2003 was not in existence on the date of filing of the 1st execution case and, as such, there is no scope to apply the provision of section 28 (4) of the Ain, 2003. he next contends that in this case the provision of section 28 (3) of the Ain, 2003 is applicable and the Bank filed the 2nd execution case within one year from the date of disposal of he 1st execution case and therefore, 2nd execution case is not barred by limitation. He lastly contends that in such view of the matter, the proceeding of the execution case as well as the impugned order passed by the learned Judge of the Adalat suffers from no legal infirmity and the rule is thus, liable to be discharged with costs. 

 12. Now let us consider whether the period of limitation as prescribed by section 28 (4) of the Ain, 2003 was applicable in the 2nd execution case. 

 ‘‘২৮। জারীর জন্য মামলা দাখিলের সময়সীমা The Limitation Act, 1908 এবং The Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 এর ভিন্নতর যে বিধানই থাকুক না কেন, ডিক্রীদার আদালতযোগে ডিক্রী বা আদেশ কার্যকর করিতে ইচ্ছা করিলে, ডিক্রী বা আদেশ প্রদত্ত হওয়ার অনুর্ধ্ব ১৮০(একশত আশি) দিবসের মধ্যে, ধারা ২৯ এর বিধান স্বাপেক্ষে জারীর জন্য আদালতে দরখাস্ত দাখিল করিয়া মামলা করিবে। 

 14. We have already noticed that the 1st execution case was filed on 14.3.2001 when the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990 (The Ain, 1990, in brief) was in force and during existence of the Ain, 1990 the provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure (the Code) was applicable relating to limitation in an execution case. 

 15. According to the provision of section 48 of the Code an application to execute a decree is to be filed within a period of 12 years and not after and this provision was applicable at the time of filing of 1st execution case on 14.3.2001. Later on, during pendency of the 1st execution case, the Ain, 2003 came into a play on 1st May, 2003 and in that view of the matter, there is no scope to give retrospective effect of the provision of section 28 (4) of the Ain, 2003 so as to apply the period of limitation in the 2nd execution case from 14.3.2001 inasmuch as the Ain, 2003 itself was not in existence on the date of filing of the 1st execution case. The provision of section 28 (4) of the Ain, 2003 can not be interpreted in such a way that section 28 (4) of the Ain, 2003 can be applied from that date of institution of the 1st execution case which was filed on 14.3.2001 long before promulgation of the Ain, 2003 (1st May, 2003). 

 16. We have carefully gone through the decisions as referred to by Mr. Barek and we find that the facts and circumstance of those cases are completely different from the facts of the present case as in the cited case the execution case was filed beyond the period of 12 years. Therefore, the execution case was also barred by limitation in view of the provision of section 48 of the Code. The judgment dated 20.4.2009 passed by our Apex Court, in the Civil Petition For Leave to Appeal No. 2180 of 2008 rather support our view inasmuch as it has been observed in this judgment as under: 

 "In the instant case the provision of the section 28 can not be applied inasmuch as the limitation of 6 years expired prior to promulgation of the new Act, Artha Rin Ain 2003. the same principle is also applicable in this case which means that section 28 (4) of the Ain, 2003 can not be applied before promulgation of the Ain, 2003."
